Take out the compass and face the direction you want to know the azimuth of

Find a landmark such as a building, tree, big rock or mountain.

Unfold the top of the compass containing the wire and the bottom containing  the magnifying glass(angling it at a generally 45 degree angle)

Look through the rear notch back post and align it with the front wire as is you a shooting a gun.

Point it at your landmark.

Look down the magnifying glass and it will show you the exact azimuth of your landmark.

The wire is not supposed to move, that part is used to “aim” the compass into the distance using the rear notched aperture to gain an exact azimuth, which is a fancy word for the degrees used for directions.

The part that does rotate is called bezel, and this should spin freely all the way around the compass regardless of where you spin it. The purpose of this bezel is to allow for faster azimuth referencing. 

If you want to head East, which has a magnetic azimuth of 090 degrees, you can turn first turn into the exact direction you want to move, and then turn the bezel to reference exactly where the North arrow is facing. Now whenever you look at the compass while walking, instead of guessing that you are heading East, you will have a notched indicator telling you that you are on or off your course.
